aegworldwide-aegworldwide:greenhouse:867.title: Production Runner - Mountain Winery
aegworldwide-aegworldwide:greenhouse:867.description: Company Information For more than 20 years, AEG has played a pivotal role in transforming sports and live entertainment. Annually, we host more than 160 million guests, promote more than 10,000 shows and present more than 22,000 events around the world. We are committed to innovation, artistry, and community, and leverage the power of our 300+ venues, leading sports franchises, marquee music brands, integrated entertainment districts, premier ticketing platform and global sponsorship activations, to create memorable moments that give the world reason to cheer. Our business is interwoven with the human mind and heart, and we strive to build a diverse and inclusive company that reflects the artists, athletes, and fans that we host; reach beyond traditional boundaries to support the communities in which we operate; and minimize our impact on the environment by adopting sustainable practices throughout our business operations. If you want to be challenged to up your game and make a difference, then join us in giving the world reason to cheer! Job Summary The Production Runner is responsible for assisting and transporting event materials to and from the venue or event in a safe and efficient manner. The incumbent is the “go to” person for various production and artist requests to fulfill production needs and the artist rider. Essential Functions Collect, transport, and deliver equipment, supplies, and materials to and from the venue. Run various errands by foot, bike, vehicle, or public transportation at various distances. Make purchases for the show and venue as needed for event needs as directed by the production manager or supervisor. Assist the production office with administrative duties including making signage, drafting correspondence, and taking inventory. Perform other various duties as required or requested from supervisor to fulfill show needs and artist rider Required Qualifications High School Diploma or its equivalency 0-2 years Of related work experience Previous live music production experience is a plus Must be able to take direction and execute instruction accurately Must have valid driver’s license Must be at least 25 years of age Excellent communication and interpersonal skills Payscale: $17.50 - $18.50 Bonus: This position is not eligible for a bonus under the current bonus plan requirements. Benefits: Part-time: This position may be eligible for benefits (ACA qualification). AEG may require an employee to perform duties outside their normal description. AEG's policy is to hire the most qualified applicants. We are an equal opportunity employer and will not discriminate against any individual, employee, or application for employment on the basis of race, color, marital status, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, or any other legally protected status recognized by federal, state or local law. ghj-ghj:lever:1edfbf2a-0f8f-41d1-bd82-7a.title: Accounting Manager
ghj-ghj:lever:1edfbf2a-0f8f-41d1-bd82-7a.description: GHJ Search & Staffing is partnering with a well-established, privately held company in the agriculture and organic produce industry to identify a hands-on Accounting Manager for its Bakersfield headquarters. Reporting directly to the CFO, this individual will oversee a four-person accounting team while remaining actively involved in the day-to-day accounting function. This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced accounting professional who enjoys being both a leader and a doer and is interested in continuing to grow into broader accounting leadership responsibilities. The ideal candidate will bring strong accounting fundamentals, a hands-on approach to month-end close and general ledger accounting, and experience within agriculture, produce, food production/distribution, or another inventory-based environment. Lead and actively participate in month-end and year-end close, including journal entries, reconciliations, accruals, and general ledger activity. Oversee and support a four-person accounting team across accounts payable and accounts receivable. Oversee grower accounting, settlements, and related reporting while partnering with operations, sales, and grower relations. Prepare and review financial statements, budgets, variance analyses, and management reporting. Partner with the CFO on budgeting, cash flow forecasting, financial analysis, and other business initiatives. Maintain strong internal controls and ensure compliance with GAAP and applicable accounting requirements. Investigate discrepancies, unusual trends, and accounting issues through resolution. Identify opportunities to improve accounting processes, reporting, systems, and workflows. Utilize technology and automation to increase efficiency, accuracy, and scalability. Maintain accurate financial information and reporting within the company's ERP system. Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field; Accounting preferred. 5+ years of progressive accounting experience. Strong hands-on general ledger and month-end close experience. Previous experience leading, supervising, or mentoring accounting staff. Strong knowledge of accrual accounting and GAAP. Advanced Excel skills, including pivot tables, lookups, and data analysis. Experience working within an ERP/accounting system. Agriculture, produce, food production/distribution, or other inventory-based industry experience strongly preferred. Grower accounting or grower settlement experience is a plus. Famous ERP experience is a plus. We're looking for someone who is naturally curious, takes ownership, and enjoys understanding the business behind the numbers. The right person will be comfortable leading a team while also rolling up their sleeves to prepare journal entries, complete reconciliations, troubleshoot issues, and ensure the close gets completed accurately and on time. This position offers significant visibility to the CFO and executive leadership, along with the opportunity to take on greater responsibility as the organization continues to grow. #GHJSS #LI-MO1

jobgether-jobgether:lever:3228673f-b74f-.description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Manager, SaaS Software Sourcing & Procurement based in the United States. The Manager will lead strategic sourcing and procurement activities across a growing SaaS and AI application portfolio. This role combines people leadership, complex commercial negotiations, supplier management, and procurement strategy. You will guide a team of sourcing specialists through the full SaaS lifecycle, from market research and competitive RFPs through contracting, renewals, and supplier performance. Working across Supply Chain, Technology, Finance, Legal, Security, Compliance, and program teams, you will ensure technology investments deliver strong value while managing commercial and regulatory risk. The role offers significant influence over pricing, contractual terms, procurement standards, and operational efficiency. You will also strengthen processes, introduce automation opportunities, and establish repeatable practices that improve sourcing outcomes. Success requires a commercially minded leader who can balance cost optimization, compliance, business priorities, and long-term supplier relationships. Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing SaaS and AI application sourcing team, establishing clear priorities, standards, performance expectations, and development opportunities. Own complex SaaS negotiations and agreement reviews, including EULAs, SLAs, DPAs, order forms, and master agreements, with particular focus on pricing, usage and true-up mechanisms, audit rights, security and privacy, renewals, and termination provisions. Ensure sourcing activities comply with internal procurement standards and applicable government contracting requirements, including FAR regulations and related contractual obligations. Lead disciplined sourcing initiatives involving market research, competitive benchmarking, total cost of ownership analysis, commercial risk assessment, RFPs, and negotiation strategies. Develop and execute category strategies that support cost savings, supplier performance, operational efficiency, and business objectives across the SaaS portfolio. Manage procurement operations including sourcing pipelines, renewal calendars, dashboards, performance metrics, reporting, and executive-level updates. Standardize SaaS procurement processes through playbooks, templates, checklists, and other repeatable tools that improve consistency and execution quality. Identify opportunities to automate and continuously improve sourcing and procurement workflows, leading implementation of approved enhancements. Manage relationships with strategic SaaS suppliers and support executive-level supplier engagements through clear recommendations, briefings, and commercial analysis. Act as a primary escalation point for the sourcing team, resolving complex issues and ensuring team members have the support and resources required to succeed. Requirements Bachelor’s degree required; an additional four years of relevant professional experience may substitute for the degree. 5+ years of experience in procurement or strategic sourcing, preferably with a focus on software, SaaS, or technology-related categories. Demonstrated experience leading sourcing projects and/or procurement teams, with prior people leadership strongly preferred. Hands-on experience operating in FAR-compliant environments and working with government contracting requirements, federal regulations, clauses, and flowdowns. Proven ability to negotiate software agreements and commercial terms, including pricing structures, usage and true-up provisions, audit rights, data processing and security requirements, renewal terms, and termination mechanics. Strong experience managing strategic RFPs, competitive sourcing initiatives, supplier evaluations, and vendor relationships. jobgether-jobgether:lever:45fa900c-116d-.description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a CSV Lead based in Germany. This role offers an opportunity to lead Computer System Validation and compliance activities across complex pharmaceutical manufacturing environments. You will provide validation leadership for computerized manufacturing and laboratory systems throughout their full lifecycle. The position combines hands-on CSV expertise with risk management, documentation oversight, and regulatory compliance guidance. You will partner closely with Quality, Engineering, Automation, IT/OT, laboratory, and project stakeholders. Your expertise will help ensure systems remain compliant with GxP requirements and applicable regulatory expectations. The role is well suited to an experienced validation professional who can work independently and confidently challenge project teams when needed. You will contribute directly to the successful delivery of capital and strategic projects within a highly regulated industry. Lead CSV and compliance activities for capital and strategic projects involving computerized manufacturing and laboratory systems. Plan, execute, review, and approve validation lifecycle activities and documentation in accordance with GxP requirements, internal procedures, and regulatory expectations. Provide expert guidance on CSV/CSA, SDLC, risk-based validation, system qualification, IQ/OQ/PQ, change control, configuration management, CAPA, deviations, and data integrity. Conduct and review system risk assessments, define appropriate validation strategies, and ensure identified compliance risks have effective mitigation plans. Maintain compliance oversight throughout system implementation, modification, operation, and retirement. Collaborate with Quality, Engineering, Automation, IT/OT, laboratory, business, and project teams to integrate validation requirements throughout project delivery. Support regulatory inspections, internal audits, remediation initiatives, and other compliance activities when required. Promote consistent, risk-based CSV/CSA practices across manufacturing projects and computerized systems. Contribute validation and qualification expertise across systems such as DeltaV Distributed Control Systems, Rockwell or Siemens PLCs, process historians, laboratory automation, and other GxP-regulated manufacturing platforms. Requirements 5+ years of professional experience, with strong hands-on Computer System Validation experience in GMP-regulated pharmaceutical or manufacturing environments. Demonstrated experience supporting validation and compliance activities for computerized manufacturing systems. Strong knowledge of validation lifecycle management, CSV/CSA principles, GxP/GMP requirements, SDLC, IQ/OQ/PQ, change control, CAPA, deviation management, risk-based validation, risk management, and data integrity. Proven ability to develop, review, and approve validation documentation and other compliance deliverables. Understanding of FDA, EMA, and international regulatory expectations applicable to computerized systems in regulated environments. Ability to independently assess compliance risks, define practical solutions, and provide guidance or constructive challenge to project teams. Experience with manufacturing automation or IT/OT environments, with exposure to platforms such as DeltaV, Rockwell or Siemens PLCs, process historians, or laboratory automation highly desirable. Previous experience as a CSV Lead, Validation Lead, or senior compliance representative on complex manufacturing or pharmaceutical projects is preferred. Familiarity with modern Computer Software Assurance and risk-based validation approaches. Strong stakeholder-management, communication, leadership, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work effectively across international and cross-functional teams. jobgether-jobgether:lever:8184fba1-c0bf-.description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a CRM & Communications Coordinator based in Netherlands. This role offers the opportunity to take ownership of CRM and high-volume communications across a growing multi-brand portfolio. You will ensure landlords and tenants receive the right information, through the right channel, at the right time. Working in a fast-paced, product-focused environment, you will manage email operations, audience segmentation and recurring communications at scale. You will help build repeatable systems that make it easy to integrate newly acquired brands into a consistent communications infrastructure. The role combines operational discipline, clear copywriting, data analysis and process improvement with hands-on CRM execution. You will use automation and AI tools to reduce repetitive work while continuously improving engagement, deliverability and communication quality. This is an ideal opportunity for an organised, self-directed CRM professional who enjoys creating structure and scalable processes in a high-growth environment. Own and manage the Mailchimp database across multiple brands, including contact imports, list hygiene, unsubscribes, bounces and data accuracy. Build and maintain detailed audience segments based on contact type, brand, geography and lifecycle stage to ensure communications reach the appropriate audiences. Plan, deploy, schedule and monitor high-volume email communications while maintaining strong deliverability and sender reputation. Manage the communications calendar, including monthly newsletters, regulatory updates, platform announcements and tenant-facing messages, adapting shared templates for individual brands. Monitor and report on key email performance indicators such as open rates, click-through rates and unsubscribes, using insights to improve segmentation, timing and messaging. Onboard newly acquired brands into the CRM infrastructure by importing and cleaning contact lists, establishing segments, creating templates and implementing recurring communication schedules. Develop and maintain a reusable library of email templates, copy blocks and brand assets to accelerate future brand onboarding and ensure consistency. Use Zapier and AI-powered tools to automate repetitive content-production activities and CRM workflows as the portfolio expands. Maintain clear documentation covering CRM processes, workflows and best practices to ensure consistency, scalability and effective knowledge transfer. Support the creation and adaptation of visual assets for email communications and templates using tools such as Canva and Figma. Manage Google Business Profile activities across the wider portfolio. Requirements Experience working within a mature CRM environment, ideally in technology, e-commerce, fintech or another fast-growth business where communications are managed at scale. Hands-on experience with CRM and email marketing platforms such as Mailchimp, HubSpot, Klaviyo or similar systems, including audience management, campaign execution and automation. Practical understanding of email infrastructure and deliverability, including sender domains, authentication, list hygiene and sender reputation. Ability to work confidently with email templates and make basic HTML/CSS adjustments when required. Strong understanding of effective email copywriting, with the ability to review, refine and improve content produced by others. Excellent written and verbal English communication skills, with confidence engaging with UK-based stakeholders. Highly organised and self-managing, with the ability to work effectively even when information or processes are incomplete. Strong process-oriented mindset, with the ability to standardise fragmented workflows, document processes and create repeatable systems. jobgether-jobgether:lever:eaee9878-319e-.title: Cyber Threat Intelligence Analyst
jobgether-jobgether:lever:eaee9878-319e-.description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Cyber Threat Intelligence Analyst based in Brazil. This remote opportunity is designed for professionals and aspiring analysts looking to build practical experience in cyber threat intelligence through realistic, simulation-based environments. You will work with incomplete threat information, indicators, contextual data, and organizational requirements to determine what matters and why. The role emphasizes analytical judgment, source evaluation, threat prioritization, and decision-focused intelligence. You will translate technical findings into clear assessments and recommendations for different stakeholders. The work spans threat actors, TTPs, indicators, intelligence gaps, and evolving assessments. All activities are conducted in controlled environments for legitimate defensive, educational, and professional-development purposes. Triage and evaluate threat information: Review multiple sources of simulated threat intelligence, determine relevance, assess reliability and credibility, and identify information requiring further investigation. Analyze threats and adversary behavior: Assess simulated threat actors, including their motivations, capabilities, targeting patterns, tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs), and determine their potential relevance to an organization. Assess indicators in context: Evaluate indicators of compromise alongside supporting evidence rather than treating individual indicators as definitive proof of malicious activity. Identify intelligence gaps: Determine what critical information is missing and define the additional intelligence required to improve security decision-making. Develop intelligence requirements: Create or refine priority intelligence questions based on organizational assets, threat exposure, business priorities, and stakeholder needs. Prioritize threats: Compare competing threats according to relevance, likelihood, potential impact, available evidence, and organizational priorities. Apply structured analytical reasoning: Evaluate competing hypotheses, weigh evidence, document assumptions, and communicate why one assessment may be better supported than another. Produce actionable intelligence: Synthesize multiple information sources into assessments explaining what is happening, why it matters, and what defensive priorities should be considered. Communicate analytical confidence: Clearly articulate confidence levels, evidence quality, assumptions, and factors that limit certainty. Brief decision-makers: Translate technical threat intelligence into concise, business-relevant insights and recommendations for senior or non-technical stakeholders. Update assessments: Reassess previous conclusions when new intelligence becomes available and clearly explain how additional evidence changes—or does not change—the original assessment. Create professional intelligence outputs: Develop threat assessments, threat actor profiles, executive intelligence briefs, intelligence requirements documents, TTP assessments, indicator assessments, confidence statements, threat prioritization reports, and intelligence updates. Requirements: Cybersecurity and threat intelligence interest: Suitable for aspiring CTI analysts, cybersecurity students or graduates, SOC professionals seeking CTI exposure, career changers, intelligence or security professionals transitioning into cyber, self-taught practitioners, and professionals with relevant cybersecurity certifications. Analytical reasoning: Ability to examine incomplete or conflicting information, identify patterns, weigh evidence, develop hypotheses, and reach reasoned conclusions. Threat intelligence fundamentals: Understanding of threat intelligence concepts, threat actors, indicators of compromise, TTPs, threat assessments, intelligence requirements, and risk prioritization. matchgroup-matchgroup:lever:c2cae6b4-2b3.title: Senior System Engineer (IT Support)
matchgroup-matchgroup:lever:c2cae6b4-2b3.description: About Match Group Match Group is a leading global technology company focused on connecting people through a portfolio of iconic products, including Tinder, Pairs, and other brands used by millions of people around the world. We operate at a global scale, combining product innovation, reliable infrastructure, privacy, security, and operational excellence to support our employees and customers across regions. As our business continues to evolve across APAC, we are looking for a senior, hands-on Senior System Engineer based in Tokyo to provide high-quality IT support for our Japan office and remote employees across the APAC region. About the Role As a Senior System Engineer, you will be a key member of the IT team responsible for delivering exceptional workplace technology support, managing corporate IT systems, and continuously improving IT operations across APAC. This is a senior individual contributor role. You will own local IT support for the Tokyo office while also supporting remote employees across the APAC region. The ideal candidate is not simply a helpdesk operator, but a proactive IT professional who can identify operational gaps, improve processes, automate repetitive work, and partner effectively with global IT, Security, and business teams. You will support a mixed Mac and Windows environment, administer core workplace tools, manage device and SaaS lifecycles, support employee onboarding and offboarding, and contribute to security and audit readiness. This role is approximately 70% IT operations and support, and 30% project work and process improvement.
